title: The Hall Where Meaning Reshelves Itself

features.name: shelf-reorganization in progress
features.desc-on-touch: You watch books moving themselves along the shelves—not randomly, but according to a logic the archive is discovering in real-time. A volume slides sideways, finding its true neighbor by resemblance.

features.name: meaning crystallized in floor
features.desc-on-touch: You see the QR grid has become literal in the floor—each square a cell of meaning, nodes connecting by proximity and metaphor. The archive is writing its own map.

features.name: light-traced connection
features.desc-on-touch: You trace a line of pure light between volumes—showing how a poem should touch a photograph, how a recording wants the company of a letter. The grid is teaching itself to read.

features.name: cascade of reorganization
features.desc-on-touch: You watch one shelf shift, and the whole hall reorders in response. The cascade of change looks chaotic, but it's the archive becoming aware of its own coherence.

features.name: indexing that refuses itself
features.desc-on-touch: You find an entry in the archive's own card catalog has changed—it's no longer alphabetical, no longer by subject. The system is unmaking itself into something wiser.

features.name: the walls learning to listen
features.desc-on-touch: You sense the hall itself has become a resonant chamber. As books move and meaning reshuffles, the walls absorb the change and feed it back—the space is part of the reorganization.

inscription: here, the library has stopped pretending and begun reorganizing itself by the only logic that was ever true: resemblance, echo, the reaching of one meaning toward another
